<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/vitest.repo-tests.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `078783dc90f3ddb55fd35e3c29a9c71070e6ba23` — the merge of head `04410745d67245dabfae35d9248876fca4f7f904` into base `87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 078783dc90f3ddb55fd35e3c29a9c71070e6ba23 && git checkout 078783dc90f3ddb55fd35e3c29a9c71070e6ba23
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f 04410745d67245dabfae35d9248876fca4f7f904 && git checkout -B drift-repro 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f && git merge --no-ff 04410745d67245dabfae35d9248876fca4f7f904

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `04410745d67245dabfae35d9248876fca4f7f904`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed against: card #23228 (body; comments `6144075528`, `6147063404`, `6153222151`; the seat ACCEPT `6153329772` read as a claim under test, not as evidence), ADR-0138 D8 and the E4 execution row on `main`, ADR-0087 (the 2026-09-13 level amendment and the disposition-vocabulary addenda), PR #23324 (body, the one PR comment, file list, the net diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head, and the head itself read by its 40-hex sha (`git show`, `git grep`). objectui read on disk at the pinned `1fb1ced36` and at its current `7578323a5`; nothing cloned, built, run or checked out.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Inside ADR-0138 D8 / E4; the 13-file surface held.** The diff retires exactly the record-share `guest` recipient: the union member in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` and the select option in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-record-share.object.ts` go together, each with a comment that holds the two equal. The four `*.objects.generated.ts` bundles lose exactly the `guest` key under `recipient_type.options` and nothing else moves in them, which is the generator's shape (merge mode keeps translated values, drops a key the source no longer declares); `pnpm check:i18n` runs inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, green on this head. No other D8 row is touched: `position.zod.ts`, `sys-audience-binding-suggestion.object.ts`, `execution-context.zod.ts`, `explain.zod.ts`, `assemble-execution-context.ts` and `rest-server.ts` are absent from the file list. The sharing-RULE vocabulary is untouched: `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts`, `security/sharing.zod.ts` and `SharingRuleRecipientType` are not in the diff; the only edit near it is a comment line in the spec contract test. Against the claim's bullets: contract union, select option, translations, pins and tests (four test files plus the `vitest.repo-tests.json` registration), the ADR-0087 marker and one changeset are all present; no docs page needed a change (`content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx:59` lists the grant's refusal reasons without naming `guest`, and no page in `content/docs` lists the record-share recipient values). The grant edit in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts`: the dev reads it as the record's pin "the value refused with its prescription". I hold that reading. The pin cannot exist without a refusal that carries a prescription, and the pre-existing generic refusal carried a misdirection for `guest` ("delivered via sharing rules", which the rule vocabulary retired in v17), so the edit is the pin's subject, not scope growth. The claim's "change no live behaviour" bullet addressed dead reader branches; the one live change is the sentence for the retired value alone, and the dev declared it. Read in the diff: the `else` arm's string is byte-identical to the old string, the `VALIDATION_FAILED:` prefix is kept on both arms, and no other value's path changes.

**(b) The row door, and a legacy `guest` row.** Measured on the head, not from the claim: (1) Update. `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts` `validateRecordInScope` walks every declared field only in `insert` mode; in `update` mode it iterates `Object.entries(data)` and validates only supplied fields ("an OMITTED field never 400s"), and every engine call site (`engine.ts:16450`, `:16642`, `:16786`, `:16909`) passes the patch (`hookContext.input.data`) in `update` mode. An update of a stored `guest` row that does not carry `recipient_type` is not refused. (2) Gates. `buildReadFilter`, `buildWriteFilter` and `checkEdit` query `sys_record_share` with `recipient_type: 'user'` (`sharing-service.ts:518`, `:594`, `:805`); a `guest` row is never consulted. (3) Revoke. `revoke()` deletes by id (system path directly; user path after `assertCanManageShares` and the `source` check) and reads no `recipient_type`; the orphan sweeps key on record ids. (4) List and explain. `listShares()` returns rows verbatim, so a legacy row surfaces with `recipient_type: 'guest'`, a value the published `RecordShare` type no longer admits (a typing gap for a TypeScript reader of that array, not a runtime fault); `plugin-security`'s explain engine renders it as kind `record_share`, `via` `guest:` plus the id, effect `neutral` (`explain-engine.ts:1488-1498`) and throws nothing; `rest-server.ts` passes `recipientType` through untouched and its `guest` reads are the `guest_portal` form doors. (5) No in-repo writer re-sends the value: the grant's update half patches level, source, reason and organization only, and the rule reconciler writes `user` rows. So the changeset's sentence "A `guest` row that a system write stored before this release is read by no gate, both before and after" is true as written. Nothing is owed for such rows under ADR-0087: a database row is data, not a stored metadata surface, which is the condition the record sets for `registered`; the row stays inert, visible in `listShares` and Setup's `all_shares` view, and revocable through the existing delete path. One cosmetic consequence, non-blocking: with the `guest` label gone from the bundles, a legacy row's `recipient_type` renders as the raw value in Setup. The disposition's "nothing to rewrite" assumption holds.

**(c) The grant door.** The refusal sentence is true: ADR-0090 D11's section says, verbatim at its rejected-alternative paragraph, that guest access flows through the guest position plus share links; share links are the real object `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-share-link.object.ts`; public forms are the real surface (`rest-server.ts` `registerFormEndpoints`, `publicFormGrant`). The `VALIDATION_FAILED:` prefix is kept, so `respondSharingError`'s `startsWith` map (`rest-server.ts:11119`) still answers 400 and strips the prefix; every other value's sentence is the old string unchanged. The `RETIRED_RECIPIENT_TYPE_REFUSALS` map plus its `hasOwnProperty`-guarded helper is more machinery than the one value needs (D8 keeps `group`, `position` and `unit_and_subordinates` as members, so no second entry is in sight); a plain equality branch would do the same. Noted only, not wrong: the helper takes `unknown`, the lookup is own-property guarded, and the generic arm is untouched.

**(d) The pins; the census radius.** Each fails on revert: (1) union: the `@ts-expect-error` assignment becomes an unused directive (TS2578) and the `Extract` equality collapses to a non-`never` member, so the `Assert` alias fails; the file is compiled by `check:test-typecheck` under `tsconfig.test.json` (`include` `src/**/*`) and is absent from `packages/spec/test-typecheck-debt.json`, so the error is live, not ledgered. (2) select: `options` equality against the four values, plus a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` insert of `guest` refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_option` / the four options and nothing stored, beside a `user` control that lands; re-offering the option fails two of three (`driver-sql` and `better-sqlite3` are plugin-sharing devDependencies, so the harness resolves in CI). (3) grant: the sentence's first clause, the D11 clause, the trailing remedy, no "sharing rules", and an empty table; dropping the arm fails the first-clause assertion. (4) census, in `test:repo`, which `Test Core` runs (`ci.yml:965`, `turbo run test test:repo`): three matchers each with planted positives and neighbour negatives (a comparison, `principalKind`, `guest_portal`, prose, a comment), lit controls on the real tree (visited above 1000, record-share files above 20, `user` producers above 20), then the sweep. Its radius is the five roots `packages`, `examples`, `skills`, `content`, `scripts` with the per-extension shape that `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` declares for `@objectstack/spec`; the comment-mask import rides `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, which has a `.d.mts` beside it and precedent in eight CLI tests. Outside the radius I grepped the whole head myself: no file anywhere spells `recipient_type` or `recipientType` as `guest` as a producer; `docs/`, `.claude/`, `.github/`, `apps/`, `patches/`, `docker/` and the root files carry only historical ADR and audit prose, and one stale sharing-RULE example (`docs/notes/crm-development-standards.mdx:291`, the `sharedWith` vocabulary `user | group | role | role_and_subordinates | guest`, retired in v17 and not a record-share recipient, not this card's). No enum list pairs `unit_and_subordinates` with `guest` outside the changeset and ADR-0111's history. No AI tool schema or service spells it. No seed targets `sys_record_share`. objectui at the pin and at its current head: zero hits for `recipient` near `guest`; `RecipientPickerField.TYPE_TO_OBJECT` maps `user`, `team`, `business_unit`, `unit_and_subordinates` plus the `position` registry, and unknown kinds degrade to a text input. The census is honest about its bound (runtime-assembled values, the out-of-radius roots), and the bound held under my own wider read.

**(e) ADR-0087 and the changeset, every sentence read.** True throughout: the four-member union; the compile error for `recipientType: 'guest'` on `GrantShareInput` and for `RecordShare.recipient_type` (both typed `RecordShareRecipientType` at the head); the four options and the dropped labels; the grant's prior refusal (ADR-0111 D7 arm); the `user`-only gates; the ADR-0090 D11 route; the v17 rule-vocabulary retirement (`17.sharing-rule-recipient-reconcile`); the 400 before and after; the row door's `invalid_option` with the four values; the unchanged set. The marker's category reasoning is correct on the gate's own grammar: `type-surface-only` is closed (the diff touches `packages/spec` and a `contracts/` file; nothing narrowed off `any`), `runtime-interface-only` is closed (declared under `contracts/`), `unpublished` is false, `registered` would write a ledger line that `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to project, and `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the category ADR-0138 D8 and the E4 row expect when the census finds no stored metadata surface. The omitted FROM/TO block is required by that category, not a shortcut: ADR-0087's addendum says the catch-all "is refused by a body that carries a migration prescription", and the gate's detector reads arrows, labelled FROM/TO and framed tables; the body carries none and states what each door answers in prose. `check-adr-0087-registration` runs in `Check Changeset` (`pr-automation.yml:980`), green on both runs. Level: pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json` mode `pre`, tag `next`); ADR-0087's 2026-09-13 amendment rules that a pre-GA retirement ships `minor` with the BREAKING banner and the disposition; both are present; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` in this window. Correct category, correct level.

**(f) The out-of-scope findings.** The `group` sentence: the generic arm says group/position recipients are delivered via sharing rules, and the rule select on the head is `user`, `team`, `business_unit`, `position`, `unit_and_subordinates`, `field`, with no `group`; the ledger entry `sharing-rule-recipient-reconcile` records the `group` to `team` rename as the ADR-0090 D3 rename (so the dev's citation is substantiated in-repo, whatever the seat could confirm). It predates this PR, this PR leaves that arm byte-identical, D8 keeps `group` as a union member, and the right wording is a choice; #23325 is the correct carrier and nothing is owed here. The no-per-option-retirement-slot observation holds on the head: `keptOptionValues` on the validator is the import runner's kept-cell channel, and `enumWithRetiredValues` attaches to a `z.enum`, which neither declaration is. Nothing is owed by this PR; see ③ for the consequence.

**(g) CI on the head, read at 2026-10-13T19:30Z.** Not green: `Test Core (1/6)` through `Test Core (6/6)` in_progress, `Type Check · workspace` in_progress; the required summary contexts `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` have not yet been produced, so this record does not vouch for them. No check has failed. Green: `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, the seven `Lint ·` jobs, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, and the PR-automation checks. Skipped by design on a PR run: `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, the Dogfood matrix shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and the second `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` runs. The docs-drift comment is advisory; none of the nine hand-written pages it lists names `guest` as a record-share recipient.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, with the BREAKING banner, the `!` in the title, the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line and the marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` in the body. That is the level ADR-0087's amended level rule assigns to a pre-GA accept-set narrowing, and the category the Accepted record names for E4 when the census finds nothing. Published surface narrowed: the `RecordShareRecipientType` union (recorded in `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, which is byte-identical, as a value narrowing must leave it) and the `recipient_type` option set of `sys_record_share`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Declared deviation, accepted:** no FROM/TO block, though the dispatch listed one. The record's expected category refuses one, and the dev chose the record and reported it. Correct precedence.
- **Declared deviation, accepted:** the grant's refusal-with-prescription edit as a live-behaviour change confined to the retired value's sentence. Prefix, status, and every other value's path unchanged, verified in the diff.
- **Non-blocking:** the one-entry `RETIRED_RECIPIENT_TYPE_REFUSALS` map is speculative infrastructure for a value class with one member; a plain branch would carry the same pin.
- **Non-blocking:** the row door's refusal lists the four legal values and carries no prescription; the prescription travels on the union's TSDoc, the grant's sentence and the changeset. A per-option retirement slot on `Field.select` would be a new mechanism outside this card; the dev named the gap rather than hand-rolling one.
- **Non-blocking:** a `guest` row stored before this release remains visible in `listShares`, Setup's `all_shares` view and explain output, under a value the published `RecordShare` type no longer admits, and renders without a label. Inert before and after; revocable.
- **Out of scope, carried elsewhere:** the `group` refusal wording (#23325); the stale sharing-RULE example in `docs/notes/crm-development-standards.mdx:291`, which names the rule vocabulary retired in v17 and is not this card's.
- **Not re-judged here:** `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` were in progress at the read; the owning seat reads them green before the queue.
